page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled directly, consisting of a 2458 GB local SSD. No GPU accelerators are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance and memory throughput. The server achieves a strong multi-core stress-ng score of 62149.0 and a strong Geekbench multi-core score of 16422.0, contrasted with average single-core performance. Large-block memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 291.88 GB/sec for read-only operations and 134.9 GB/sec for write operations. The processor supports AVX-512 vector extensions, contributing to strong scores in Passmark extended instructions and encryption tests. Additionally, the system demonstrates strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 294.99 GB/sec and strong database operations.

From a resource density perspective, the D64d_v5 offers a balanced allocation of compute and memory alongside a high-capacity local SSD. This bundled storage reduces the need for external block storage attachments for temporary data, enhancing qualitative cost efficiency for disk-intensive workloads. However, a key tradeoff is the average single-core performance and average LLM inference speeds, which may limit its suitability for latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks or heavy AI model generation workloads.

This server is configured for workloads that benefit from high multi-threaded concurrency and local storage capacity. Appropriate applications include database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression.
